prs.title: fix(reporters): junit to strip ANSI sequences from all XML attributes
prs.author: meganemura
prs.body:
### Description

The JUnit reporter strips ANSI sequences from the `<failure>` body, but not from attribute values. `escapeXML` removes the ESC byte because XML cannot hold it, but the rest of each sequence stays. An error message that has colors (for example, the DOM dump that Testing Library adds by default) gives:

```xml
<failure message="[36m<body>[39m" type="Error">
```

CI tools that show the `message` attribute then print `[36m` as text.

This PR strips ANSI sequences in `escapeXML`. The `message` attribute, the `name` of unhandled-error test cases, and `system-out` / `system-err` now get the same treatment as the `<failure>` body.

AI disclosure: I used Claude Code to investigate and write this change.

prs.title: fix(pretty-format): support boxed symbols (fix #11445)
prs.author: lehni
prs.body:
### Description

Fixes #11445

`printSymbol()` used `String(val)`, which throws `TypeError: Cannot convert a Symbol value to a string` for boxed symbols (`Object(Symbol('a'))`). They reach it through the `[object Symbol]` branch of `printBasicValue()`. Using `Symbol.prototype.toString.call(val)` works for both primitive and boxed symbols.

Regression from #9609 (v5): boxed symbols formatted fine with loupe in v4.

Added a `boxed symbol` test to `test/unit/test/pretty-format.test.ts`. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

AI-assisted (Claude Code).

prs.title: fix(expect): fix `Map` and `Set` deep equality in some assertions
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11296

Several matchers compared values without the `toEqual` tester list (`[...customTesters, iterableEquality]`), so any two Maps or any two Sets compared equal, and some also ignored `expect.addEqualityTesters`. This PR makes them use the same deep equality mechanism as `toEqual`.

| Matcher | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toEqual`, `toHaveBeenCalledWith` family, `toThrow(error)`, `vi.when` | ✅ `toEqual` testers | unchanged |
| `expect.objectContaining` / `arrayContaining` / `expect.extend` matchers like `expect.toBeOneOf` (#6825, #11401) | ✅ outer matcher's testers | unchanged |
| `toContainEqual`, `toHaveProperty`, `toBeOneOf` | ❌ registered testers only | ✅ `toEqual` testers |
| `toHave(Last\|Nth)?(Returned\|Resolved)With` | ❌ no testers | ✅ `toEqual` testers |
| `toThrow(asymmetricMatcher)` | ❌ no testers | ✅ `toEqual` testers |

```ts
// passes before this PR, fails after
expect([new Set(['y'])]).toContainEqual(new Set(['x']))
expect(new Set(['y'])).toBeOneOf([new Set(['x'])])
const fn = vi.fn(() => new Set(['y']))
fn()
expect(fn).toHaveReturnedWith(new Set(['x']))
```

Additionally, the docs for `toBeOneOf`, the return/resolved matchers, and `vi.when` now say they use `toEqual` equality.

TBD
- Is this a breaking change?
  - technically in the same category as [#6825](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/6825), but we can also say this fixes remaining inconsistency of 6825 and 11401.

prs.title: fix(ui): simplify explorer filtering + fix nested tests when search matches a suite
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11260

The explorer tree filtering had grown into several complicated layers with global ref and generator, so this PR takes on a larger cleanup to establish a simpler pipeline. While doing this, I also found a minor issue with the expand toggle during search and fixed it. See the html artifact https://gisthost.github.io/?3cbab4603b1f5c72b83b78aafc228456/vitest-pr-11262-explain-diff.html for the high-level idea of the change.

The bug shows up when a search matches a suite with nested suites. For example, searching `nested failure` in the fixture `test/ui/fixtures/main/suite-report.test.ts` should give a tree like:

```
_nested failure_ suite        ← search matches
  failing nested suite
    failing nested child
```

but on `main` it gives:

```
_nested failure_ suite        ← search matches
  failing nested suite        ← shown with no tests under it
```

and collapsing and expanding `failing nested suite` doesn't bring `failing nested child` back. This PR shows the full tree in both cases.

This coverage is added in e2e.

prs.title: fix(ui): store module graph once per environment
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- closes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9763
- repro: https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/ced83dcb817ffd8e96025b898edc0dc4

The html reporter stored a full `ModuleGraphData` per test file, so the report grew with test files × modules. It got slow and large, and eventually crashed `flatted.stringify` with `RangeError: Invalid string length`. This PR stores the module graph once per project and environment instead.

Report size on main grows with test files × modules, while with this PR it only grows with modules. Repro with 1000 test files that all import a shared graph of N modules:

| repro | html report size | `--merge-reports` + html |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1000 modules, 1000 test files | 140 MB → **2.0 MB** | |
| 3000 modules, 1000 test files | 421 MB → **2.6 MB** | 7.3s, 3.1 GB RSS → **0.6s, 199 MB** |
| 5000 modules, 1000 test files | crash → **3.2 MB** | crash → **0.7s, 238 MB** |

prs.title: fix(runner): don't cache failed fixture setups (fix #11237)
prs.author: hamed-bavar
prs.body:
### Description

Resolves #11237

A fixture whose setup throws stays marked as resolved, so setup never runs again.

Test scope: the mark in `cachedFixtures` is now removed when setup throws, so `retry` re-runs it. File and worker scope: the cached promise is now deleted in a `.finally` instead of a `.then`, so a rejection is not handed to the next test or the next file.

No change on the success path.

### Tests

A unit test for retry, and an e2e file with a file-scoped fixture that recovers on retry and a worker-scoped one that no longer poisons the next file. All three fail on main. The e2e cases are in a new file because `scoped-fixtures.test.ts` skips under rolldown. Existing fixture suites pass on Vite 8 and Vite 7.

I used Claude Code while investigating this. I reproduced the bugs and reviewed the fix myself.

prs.title: fix: refactor caching, fix `:` in project and change the shape of `results` cache
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
This PR:

- unifies caching into a single `VitestCache` class with subclasses for results/modules
- fix cache checks if project has `:` in the name
- accepts `cache` only as a boolean (only affects results cache though - maybe a better name like `fsModuleCache` is needed)
- makes read/write faster

Step | Old build  | Optimized
-- | -- | --
Update + write, 2,000 files | 6.2 ms | 4.2 ms
Update + write, 10,000 files | 29 ms | 20 ms
Sort with results, 2,000 files | 71 ms | 2.2 ms
Sort with results, 10,000 files | 461 ms | 11 ms
Sort without results, 10,000 files | 486 ms | 27 ms
Rerun of 1 file, 2,000 files | 49 ms  | 45.8 ms
Rerun of 1 file, 10,000 files | 75.5 ms | 58.5 ms

Changes are backwards compatible and will help with implementing `--stale`

prs.title: fix(typecheck): use typescript pool in toTestSpecification
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`toTestSpecification()` passed `'typecheck'` as the pool for typecheck modules, but the pool is called `'typescript'`.

`TestSuite` and `TestCase` also read `meta.typecheck` from their own task. Only the file task has this flag, so their specifications got the runtime pool of the project.
